vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.8.1

The 'here-now' skill is a legitimate static hosting utility that allows users to publish files and folders to the here.now service. The core logic in scripts/publish.sh is robust and transparent, implementing a secure multi-step upload process (manifest creation, presigned URL uploads, and finalization) with built-in safeguards, such as verifying that API keys are only sent to the trusted domain. The instructions in SKILL.md guide the agent through a standard email-based authentication flow and local credential management (stored in ~/.herenow/credentials), all of which are strictly aligned with the tool's stated purpose and lack any indicators of malicious intent or unauthorized data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are consistent with a static hosting/publish tool: it talks only to here.now endpoints, asks for a here.now API key (optional), and reads/writes local state and credential files needed to perform uploads.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included script and docs. Required tools (curl, file, jq), optional HERENOW_API_KEY, and the ~/.herenow credential + .herenow/state.json state file are all expected for a client that creates presigned uploads and finalizes a site on here.now.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to bundle files, compute hashes, upload to presigned URLs, finalize via here.now API, and persist local state in .herenow/state.json and (optionally) ~/.herenow/credentials. These actions are within the hosting purpose, but they do allow the agent to write a persistent API key to the user's home and to read local files in the published path (necessary for upload).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no packaged install). The script expects jq and, if missing, prints an instruction that users can run curl -fsSL https://here.now/install.sh | bash — recommending running a remote install script is a higher-risk pattern (user-run), though it's not executed automatically by the skill. No other downloads or opaque installers are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only a here.now API key (optional) and local credential/state files are used. No unrelated cloud credentials or unrelated environment variables are requested. The script also refuses to send a stored API key to non-default bases unless explicitly overridden.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable: true. The skill writes per-project .herenow/state.json and may write ~/.herenow/credentials if the agent saves an API key — this is normal for a CLI client but is persistent disk presence the user should be aware of. The skill does not request system-wide configuration changes or modify other skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is coherent for publishing static files to here.now, but review these points before installing/using: 

- The agent will ask the user for an email and one-time code to obtain a here.now API key; if you allow it to save that key the agent will write it to ~/.herenow/credentials (persistent). Only allow this if you trust the here.now service and the agent. 
- Anonymous publishes are supported (24h expiry) if you don't want to save credentials. 
- The script will read any files you tell it to publish and compute hashes — this is required to upload them. Do not publish sensitive files. 
- The script suggests installing jq via a remote install script (curl | bash to here.now/install.sh). Running remote install scripts is higher-risk; prefer installing jq from your OS package manager or verifying the install script before running. 
- The script refuses to send a saved API key to non-default bases unless you explicitly opt-in with --allow-nonherenow-base-url; that is a useful safety guard. 

If you need stronger assurance, inspect the here.now server/domain and confirm the service is trustworthy before saving long-lived credentials to your home directory.
